bugs.name: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
bugs.disease: Urethral discharge with diplococci inside neutrophils
bugs.micro: Gram-negative diplococci with flattened adjacent sides, seen inside neutrophils on a urethral smear; fastidious, needs chocolate or Thayer-Martin agar; pili and Opa proteins attach and drive uptake; pili vary too fast for lasting immunity
bugs.presentation: 22-year-old man 4 days after sex with a new partner: severe burning on urination and a copious thick yellow-white discharge soaking his underwear. Meatus red and everted; no joint pain or rash; urine nucleic acid testing is positive and his partner is treated too.

bugs.name: Chlamydia trachomatis
bugs.disease: Scant watery urethral discharge with sterile pyuria
bugs.micro: Obligate intracellular organism that cannot make its own ATP; wall lacks muramic acid; an inert infectious body enters by endocytosis, then a reticulate body divides in a vacuole; glycogen inclusions stain brown with iodine; urine NAAT
bugs.presentation: 26-year-old man with 10 days of mild burning on urination and a scant clear mucoid discharge noticed only in the morning. Urethral smear: many neutrophils and no organisms; urine 20 WBC/hpf with sterile bacterial culture; his female partner has no symptoms at all.

bugs.name: Trichomonas vaginalis
bugs.disease: Frothy yellow-green discharge with pinpoint cervical bleeding
bugs.micro: Flagellated protozoan that exists only as a motile pear-shaped trophozoite with no cyst stage; 4 anterior flagella, undulating membrane and a stiff axostyle; seen darting on a wet mount; the only internal parasite spread by sex
bugs.presentation: 31-year-old woman with 2 weeks of itching, soreness, burning on urination and a copious frothy yellow-green discharge with a foul smell. Speculum exam shows pinpoint areas of bleeding on the cervix; a wet mount of the discharge shows pear-shaped organisms darting about.

bugs.name: Staphylococcus epidermidis
bugs.micro: Gram-positive cocci in clusters; catalase-positive but coagulase-negative, non-hemolytic, does not ferment mannitol, novobiocin-sensitive; a skin commensal of everyone; builds a slimy biofilm on hardware, which usually must be removed
bugs.presentation: 59-year-old woman on home parenteral nutrition through a tunnelled line for 8 months: 5 days of low-grade fever to 38.2 C and malaise, feeling worse during each infusion; the exit site looks clean. Two of four bottles drawn from the line grow the same organism at 36 hours.

bugs.name: Enterococcus faecium
bugs.disease: Vancomycin-resistant bacteremia in a long-stay ICU patient
bugs.micro: Gram-positive cocci in pairs and short chains; catalase-negative; blackens bile esculin agar, grows in 6.5% NaCl, PYR-positive, optochin-resistant; intrinsically resistant to cephalosporins; vanA/vanB swap D-Ala-D-Ala for D-Ala-D-Lac
bugs.presentation: 66-year-old man in his fifth ICU week after bowel surgery, treated with cefepime and then vancomycin: T 38.8 C, BP 92/58. Blood cultures grow catalase-negative cocci in chains that blacken bile esculin agar, grow in 6.5% salt, and are resistant to vancomycin and ampicillin.
